sources.name: Stack Overflow Developer Survey (2023, 2024, 2025)
sources.population: Employed survey respondents; self-selected, developer-heavy; not a probability sample
sources.definition: Uses AI tools in the development process (2025: daily, weekly or monthly/infrequently)

sources.name: Real-Time Population Survey (St. Louis Fed / FRED)
sources.limitation: Smallest occupation unit is SOC major group 15 (all computer and mathematical occupations)

sources.name: HN 'Who is hiring?' ads expecting AI-tool use
sources.population: Tech companies posting on Hacker News
sources.definition: Ad expects the hire to use AI tools
sources.limitation: What employers ask for, not whether they deployed AI in the occupation's work

sources.name: Anthropic Economic Index (release 2026-06-26)
sources.definition: Percentile of observed Claude work usage for the occupation's tasks
sources.limitation: Exposure, not adoption: never shown as a share of workers

not_found.employer_deployment_by_occupation: No source found that measures whether employers deploy AI in a given occupation's work. Firm surveys (Census BTOS, OECD ICT surveys) report whether a firm uses AI at all, which cannot be split by occupation without assumptions. The page shows an ads-based proxy instead and labels it as such.
not_found.worker_usage_forecast: Not published. Three annual Stack Overflow readings (wording and occupation categories changed in 2025) cannot identify a trend; the quarterly RPS series covers a whole occupation group, not one occupation.
